newsitem.title: USA: Orlando-Orange Cty, Fla., authority disputes audit.
newsitem.headline: Orlando-Orange Cty, Fla., authority disputes audit.

text.p: The executive director of Florida's Orlando-Orange County Expressway Authority said the authority is in excellent financial shape and should not have appeared on a state auditor's list of districts that have financial emergencies.

"We really couldn't be in better financial health. We are in anything but a financial emergency," said Executive Director Harold Worrall, who blamed a misunderstanding about the agency's new accounting methods.

In an Oct 25 letter to Gov Lawton Chiles, the Florida auditor general's office listed the authority among 17 local government entities with budget deficits. The auditors said the authority had "unreserved retained earning deficits" of $27.6 million for fiscal 1994 and $45.7 million for fiscal 1995, and had no apparnet resources to cover them.

Worral said the authority switched from governmental fund accounting, or cash-based, to enterprise fund accounting, which requires it to depreciate its assets. The system's sole assets are about $1 billion worth of toll roads and rights of way.
"In my view, it's not a decpreciable item. In fact, it appreciates," Worrall said.
Additionally, the new accounting method required the authority to write off principle and interest costs from a bond refinancing last year, which acheived a present value savings of $43 million.
"It was a good thing to do," Worrall said. However, "It shows up on the bottom line as a negative."
Worrall said authority revenues rose 12 percent in 1995, to $84 million, and are projected to rise by 16 percent, to $94 million, this year.
The authority has $915 million of revenue bond debt outstanding and projects annual debt service will peak in 1999 at $6.7 million.
Worrall said most Florida toll agencies would have to switch to the new accounting method in the next two years.
"I'm amazed that there was this confusion at the state level," he said.
State auditors were not immediately available for comment.
